note: The 1849 camp itself lives in src/lib/townWalk.ts (shared with the pixel walk). This file holds the YEAR: the 'later' explore attractions, drawn at eye level as labelled absence. The Kit Carson marker is a 1937 plaque at Hwy 26 & Main — a later site here, and never a campsite or a cemetery. x/y are the painted-face percentages from TOWN_HOTSPOTS; the tile is an authored overlay, not a survey.
may: flour and rope on a pack road the native camps already knew
canvas and brush shelters at the crossing
named Northern Sierra Miwok presence as diplomacy, not a raid table
sources: West Point, Calaveras County — California Historical Landmark No. 268, registered 1937; named by tradition for Kit Carson's 1844 search for a Sierra pass. The MARKER stands at the corner of Highway 26 and Main Street.
A trading post and a crossroads of Native American trading routes before the gold; a north branch of the emigrant road came into town.
Sandy Gulch: worked from the earliest seasons of the rush; the quartz mine, the headframe and the mills that failed on sulfide ore are later (explore attraction wp_sandy_gulch, period 'later').
Willows on Main, the general store front and the Main Street boardwalk are all later (explore attractions, period 'later').
